featured.title: Meta Just Hired an Indian Founder to Run WhatsApp. The $900 Million Beside It Tells You Why.
featured.excerpt: Kunal Shah leaves CRED to lead the world's biggest messaging app, as Meta takes a 20% stake in his fintech and bets that India holds the key to WhatsApp's next chapter.
featured.image_caption: Kunal Shah, founder of CRED, who will become the global head of Meta-owned WhatsApp (Wikimedia Commons)
featured.nri_angle: An Indian founder now runs the app that connects the diaspora to home — and Meta's bet that an India playbook can monetize WhatsApp globally puts NRI engineers and the India-first product thesis at the center of Silicon Valley.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Released the Results of the Exam That Decides a Million College Futures
news.excerpt: The National Testing Agency declared the CUET UG 2026 scorecards on Tuesday for the roughly 1.16 million students who sat the country's single largest gateway to central-university seats — and for the first time, the number of women taking it has drawn almost level with men, a quiet shift that the diaspora's own college-bound families will feel directly.
news.image_caption: A university campus in India; the NTA declared CUET UG 2026 results on June 23 for roughly 1.16 million candidates
news.nri_angle: CUET is increasingly the door diaspora families' own children walk through for an Indian undergraduate education, and NRI/OCI applicants are measured against the same scorecard and the same fast-moving counselling calendar that the NTA's results just set in motion — a deadline that does not bend for families operating across time zones.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Rewrote the Rules on Foreign Money for Its Charities — and Diaspora Donors Are in the Frame
news.excerpt: A new Home Ministry notification forces NGOs to name the ultimate source behind donor-advised funds and intermediary vehicles, bars most foreign nationals from running them, and excludes proselytisation — tightening the pipe through which billions in diaspora generosity reaches India each year.
news.image_caption: A government building in New Delhi; the Union Home Ministry tightened FCRA foreign-funding rules for NGOs in a June 2026 gazette notification
news.nri_angle: NRIs and OCIs are among the largest sources of the foreign contributions these rules govern — much of it flowing through the donor-advised funds and intermediary platforms the new disclosure rule targets — so diaspora donors should expect Indian charities to now name them as the ultimate source, and will increasingly need to verify a charity's FCRA compliance before they give.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Is Buying More Russian Oil Than Ever Before — Even After Washington Pulled the Permission Slip
news.excerpt: Russian crude is set to hit a record of around 2.55 million barrels a day in June, close to half of everything India imports, as the Iran war and the scramble around the Strait of Hormuz push the world's third-largest oil buyer back to Moscow's discounted barrels — with consequences that reach the diaspora's fuel bills, flight fares and remittances.
news.image_caption: An oil tanker at sea; India's Russian crude imports are set for a record ~2.55 million barrels a day in June, nearly half of all its oil imports
news.nri_angle: Cheaper crude keeps a lid on India's fuel costs, import bill and the rupee that NRIs remit into, while India's deepening reliance on Russian oil is exactly the friction hanging over the India–U.S. trade talks that shape H-1B visas and student flows — and a live signal for the millions of Indians working the Gulf's energy economy.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Biggest Stock Exchange Is Finally Going Public — in What Would Be the Country's Largest IPO Ever
news.excerpt: After nearly a decade of delays, the National Stock Exchange has filed papers for a roughly Rs 30,000-crore listing that could value the world's busiest derivatives bourse near $57 billion. It is a pure cash-out for global funds and Indian institutions — and a long-awaited window for the diaspora investors who power so much of India's market.
news.image_caption: Mumbai's financial district; the National Stock Exchange has filed for a ~Rs 30,000-crore IPO that would be India's largest-ever
news.nri_angle: NSE is the marketplace nearly every India-focused fund, GIFT City vehicle and NRI trade runs across, so owning a slice is a bet on Indian capital markets themselves — and the global funds cashing out (Temasek, CPPIB) and the discount they accept set a price marker diaspora investors will study when one of India's two mega-IPOs of the year finally opens.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India and China Say Their Ties Are 'Normalising' Again. The Diaspora Has Heard This Before.
news.excerpt: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Delhi on Monday — Wang's first India visit since August 2025 — and both sides called the talks 'constructive and forward-looking.' Behind the diplomatic language sit the flights, visas and business links the 2020 border clash froze, and that the diaspora still navigates around.
news.image_caption: India's National Security Adviser Ajit Doval, who met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Delhi as both sides cited 'gradual normalisation'
news.nri_angle: A genuine India–China thaw would restore the direct flights, business and tourist visas and student exchanges that the 2020 border clash froze — the everyday plumbing millions in the diaspora have routed around for five years — and ease the fear that a fresh flare-up could again strand travellers and freeze trade overnight.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Economy Is Still Growing Fast. The Mood of the People Running It Just Hit a Four-Year Low.
news.excerpt: A closely watched survey shows India's private sector expanded at its slowest pace in three months in June, hiring at its weakest in half a year, and business confidence at goods producers sinking to its gloomiest in nearly four years — a cooling that lands just as the diaspora's portfolios and remittances flow back into the country.
news.image_caption: Mumbai's financial district; India's private-sector growth slowed to a three-month low in June as business confidence fell near a four-year low
news.nri_angle: The cooling lands just as foreign money — including the India-focused funds and GIFT City vehicles many NRIs invest through — flows back into a market rallying on cheaper oil, even as hiring weakens; that gap between a roaring index and cautious boardrooms is exactly what catches diaspora retail investors offside and eventually shows up in the jobs and remittances their families depend on.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: SpaceX Just Had the Second-Biggest One-Day Wipeout in US Market History. A Lot of Indian Portfolios Felt It.
news.excerpt: The most hyped IPO ever erased $400.8 billion in a single session on Monday, sliding below its debut-day close — and because the stock auto-joins the Nasdaq-100, the pain reaches index funds and pensions far beyond Elon Musk's orbit, including the diaspora's.
news.image_caption: A SpaceX rocket launch; the company's shares posted their worst day since its record June 12 IPO, shedding $400.8 billion
news.nri_angle: SpaceX auto-joins the Nasdaq-100 under Nasdaq's fast-entry rule, so its record one-day plunge flows straight into the index funds, ETFs and US retirement accounts that millions of Indian-Americans and globally-invested NRIs hold — making a single volatile rocket stock a real line item in diaspora savings.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Re-Ran Its Biggest Medical Exam to Restore Trust. Police Arrested 30 People for Rigging It Anyway.
news.excerpt: The NEET-UG was held again on Sunday after the original May test was scrapped over a paper leak. By Monday, Bihar police had busted an interstate 'solver gang' — nine MBBS students hired as proxies, 18 biometric-verification staff, and deals worth up to ₹12 lakh a seat.
news.image_caption: Students at an examination centre in India; Bihar police arrested 30 over a solver-gang racket during the NEET-UG re-exam
news.nri_angle: Many NRI families still steer children toward an affordable, merit-based MBBS in India through NEET, and children of overseas Indians with Indian citizenship sit the very same exam — so a solver-gang scandal on the re-test meant to restore trust strikes directly at the fairness that makes a medical education back home worth the bet.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America Just Lifted Iran's Oil Sanctions for 60 Days. For India, the Relief Is Already Floating Through Hormuz.
news.excerpt: After the first round of talks under a fragile peace deal, the US Treasury waived sanctions on Iran from Monday, oil resumed its slide below $80, and tankers began moving again through the world's most important oil chokepoint — the one through which two-thirds of India's crude flows.
news.image_caption: A US Navy frigate escorts an oil tanker in the Gulf; tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz resumed on June 22, 2026
news.nri_angle: India imports about 90% of its crude and routes two-thirds of it through the Strait of Hormuz, so a sanctions waiver that calms the Gulf, reopens tanker traffic and pushes oil below $80 directly eases the import bill, the rupee and inflation that shape NRI remittances and investments — while a safer strait protects the roughly 300,000 Indian seafarers who crew the world's shipping.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: After Pulling a Record $30 Billion Out of India, Foreign Investors Just Made Their Biggest Bet Back in Months
news.excerpt: Overseas funds bought more Indian stocks in a single session on Friday than on any day since early February, and the Sensex and Nifty logged a sixth gain in seven sessions — a turn that matters to every NRI with money in Indian markets.
news.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai; foreign investors made their biggest single-day purchase of Indian stocks since February
news.nri_angle: NRIs are direct stakeholders in Indian equities — the 2026 budget doubled their Portfolio Investment Scheme limit to 10% and raised the aggregate cap to 24% — so a turn in foreign flows after a record $30.6 billion exodus directly affects the value of diaspora portfolios and the rupee in which they invest and remit.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America's Top Trade Envoy Lands in Delhi Tuesday. India Wants a Better Deal Than Its Rivals — and an Apology at Sea.
news.excerpt: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer arrives for two days of talks as New Delhi pushes for a tariff edge over Vietnam and other Asian economies. The negotiations are unfolding under the shadow of three Indian sailors killed in US strikes in the Gulf.
news.image_caption: A container terminal; the US Trade Representative arrives in New Delhi for two days of trade talks
news.nri_angle: A US-India trade pact giving Indian goods a competitive edge would strengthen the business and professional ties Indian-American entrepreneurs and the tech sector depend on, even as the deaths of three Indian seafarers in US Gulf strikes force the diaspora to watch New Delhi balance courting Washington on trade with demanding accountability for its citizens.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Britain Is About to Change Prime Ministers Again. Its 1.9 Million Indians Have a Stake in Who's Next.
news.excerpt: Keir Starmer resigned on Monday, the sixth UK prime minister in a decade, with Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham the clear frontrunner to replace him within weeks. For Britain's largest ethnic minority — and for a freshly-in-force India-UK trade deal — the succession is more than a Westminster drama.
news.image_caption: 10 Downing Street in London; Keir Starmer resigned as prime minister on June 22, 2026
news.nri_angle: People of Indian origin are Britain's largest ethnic minority at close to 1.9 million, so a change of prime minister — just as the India-UK trade deal with its new professional-visa routes enters into force on July 15 — directly shapes the immigration climate, economic ties and political influence the British-Indian community depends on.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: They Grew Up American. At 21, the Law Says They Have to Leave.
news.excerpt: An estimated 250,000 'Documented Dreamers' — many of them the children of Indian professionals on work visas — face self-deportation when they turn 21 and age out of their parents' green-card line. A renewed push for the bipartisan America's CHILDREN Act is the diaspora's last, narrow hope.
news.image_caption: The US Capitol; a renewed push for the bipartisan America's CHILDREN Act seeks to protect young 'Documented Dreamers' from aging out
news.nri_angle: An estimated 250,000 'Documented Dreamers' — a disproportionate share of them children of Indian H-1B and other work-visa holders trapped in a green-card backlog of more than 1.2 million Indians — face losing legal status and self-deporting the day they turn 21, making the America's CHILDREN Act the most intimate immigration fight the diaspora faces because it is about its own US-raised children.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Washington Just Moved to End the Open-Ended Student Visa. India's 360,000 Students Are First in Line.
news.excerpt: The White House budget office has cleared a DHS rule that would scrap the decades-old 'Duration of Status' system for fixed admission terms and halve the post-study grace period to 30 days. Indian students, the largest international cohort in the US, stand to be hit hardest.
news.image_caption: Stanford University campus; a proposed U.S. rule would replace the open-ended F-1 student visa with fixed admission terms.
news.nri_angle: Indians are the largest international student population in the US at roughly 360,000, many in multi-year doctoral and research programmes, so a rule scrapping open-ended F-1 'Duration of Status' for fixed 2-4 year terms and halving the post-study grace period to 30 days strikes at a defining diaspora aspiration and the study-to-work-to-green-card pathway thousands of NRI families depend on.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America Just Proposed Making Citizenship Cost $1,330 — and Killing the Discount for Those Who Can't Pay
news.excerpt: A new DHS rule would raise the naturalization fee by about 75% and scrap the waivers and reduced rates that lower-income applicants rely on. Indians are the second-largest group of new US citizens, and tens of thousands of green-card holders are now staring at a steeper price for the last step.
news.image_caption: New citizens raise their hands to take the oath of allegiance at a 2025 US naturalization ceremony
news.nri_angle: Indians are the second-largest group of new US citizens (49,700 naturalized in FY2024) and the second-biggest foreign-born population at ~2.8 million, so a proposed near-doubling of the naturalization fee and the end of low-income and over-65 waivers lands directly on tens of thousands of Indian green-card holders weighing the final step to a US passport.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Washington Just Cleared $482 Million to Keep India's Apaches and Big Guns Firing — Days Before the Trade Fight Resumes
news.excerpt: The Pentagon's security agency has formally notified Congress of a sustainment package for India's AH-64E Apache helicopters and M777 howitzers. The defense relationship keeps deepening even as tariffs, a stalled trade deal and the deaths of three Indian sailors strain the wider partnership.
news.image_caption: An Indian Air Force AH-64E Apache attack helicopter in flight; Washington has notified a $482 million package to sustain India's Apache and M777 fleets
news.nri_angle: The US-India strategic partnership is the framework that shapes H-1B policy, investment and how the two governments treat each other's citizens, and the defense track has been its most reliable engine — so a $482M sustainment package clearing just as trade talks teeter signals to the diaspora that the strategic floor under the relationship is holding even when the commercial side stalls.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Central Bank Just Made the Diaspora an Offer It Has Used Only Once Before. NRI Deposit Rates Are Now Near 7%.
news.excerpt: To steady a sliding rupee, the Reserve Bank of India is absorbing the cost of currency risk on fresh NRI dollar deposits and freeing banks from reserve rules — the same playbook that pulled in tens of billions in 2013. Banks are racing to pass the windfall to non-resident Indians.
news.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India's headquarters in Mumbai; the central bank is courting non-resident Indian deposits to steady the rupee
news.nri_angle: The RBI's drive deliberately targets non-resident Indians' savings: FCNR(B) and NRE deposit rates near 7% with the central bank absorbing currency-hedging risk make this one of the rare times India is paying a premium specifically to win diaspora money — and the offer expires September 30.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Hackers Just Dumped 200,000 Files From an Indian Apple Supplier. Some Are Marked 'Trade Secret.'
news.excerpt: Tata Electronics, the Tata group's bet on making India the world's iPhone workshop, has confirmed a cyber breach after a ransomware crew posted purported Apple and Tesla design documents on the dark web. The leak lands at the most sensitive possible moment for India's manufacturing ambitions.
news.image_caption: Bombay House, the Tata group's Mumbai headquarters; Tata Electronics confirmed a cyber breach affecting customer data
news.nri_angle: India's bid to become the world's electronics workshop — a source of pride and jobs for the diaspora and a magnet for Indian-origin tech talent — rests on convincing Apple and Tesla their designs are safe in India, and a leak carrying customer confidentiality stamps strikes directly at that promise.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Has 31 Million People Abroad. Until This Week, It Didn't Have a Working Phone Book.
nri-world.excerpt: Delhi's new Global Pravasi Rishta portal isn't a grievance desk — it's the diaspora register the government wished it had during every recent overseas crisis.
nri-world.nri_angle: A single MEA portal that lets every NRI, OCI and PIO register once with their local Indian mission — for event invites, scheme info, and faster contact in a crisis or evacuation.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian-Americans Are 1.5% of the Country. They Pay 5-6% of Its Income Taxes.
nri-world.excerpt: A first-of-its-kind Indiaspora report puts hard numbers on diaspora success — and arrives just as the community's place in US politics turns contentious.
nri-world.image_caption: A culturally diverse team in a business meeting
nri-world.nri_angle: A data-driven case for belonging: the report reframes Indian-American immigration debates in the language of net fiscal and economic contribution, just as H-1B scrutiny intensifies.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Diaspora Used to Ask Britain to Let It In. This Week It Hosted the Conversation in the House of Lords.
nri-world.excerpt: A 'Viksit Bharat 2047' forum in Parliament's upper chamber showed how far Britain's Indians have travelled — and how much now rides on a trade deal that keeps slipping.
nri-world.image_caption: The House of Lords chamber in the Palace of Westminster, London
nri-world.nri_angle: Britain's Indian community is now its most economically successful minority; an event in the House of Lords about India's 2047 vision marks the moment that success starts converting into political voice — with the stalled India-UK FTA the real test of whether the 'living bridge' becomes infrastructure.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Wants the Diaspora's Dollars Back. It's Offering 7.1% — and a $55 Billion Bet — to Get Them.
nri-world.excerpt: A revived RBI swap scheme has touched off an FCNR deposit rate war. For NRIs the returns are real, but the fine print on lock-ins and tax is where the deal is won or lost.
nri-world.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
nri-world.nri_angle: The RBI's FCNR(B) swap subsidy is, in effect, a fundraising drive aimed squarely at the 35-million-strong diaspora's savings — offering tax-advantaged dollar returns up to 7.1%, but with three-to-five-year lock-ins and FATCA/FBAR/TDS complications that NRIs must weigh before chasing the headline rate.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Britain Spent Years Talking About Its Minorities as One Block. A New Report Says the Indians Quietly Walked Off With the Trophy.
nri-world.excerpt: A Policy Exchange study names British Indians the country's most successful ethno-religious group — 71% own their homes — and warns the political class it is reading the diaspora wrong.
nri-world.image_caption: Belgrave Road in Leicester, long a hub of Britain's Indian community, which a new report calls one of the country's most successful ethno-religious groups (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: For 1.9 million British Indians, the report is both flattering and double-edged: it confirms a generational success story while flagging that 'model minority' framing can flatten internal differences and turn a community into a political bargaining chip.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A New Mandir Opens in Oxford This Weekend. Getting There Took Years, a King's Message, and a Lot of Volunteers With Orange Lanyards.
nri-world.excerpt: The Oxford Hindu Mandir & Community Centre holds its grand opening on June 21, the latest sign that the diaspora is building permanent institutions, not just renting halls.
nri-world.image_caption: A Hindu mandir in Britain; Oxford's new Hindu Mandir & Community Centre opens this weekend after years of community fundraising (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: For Oxford's Hindu families, a purpose-built mandir replaces decades of borrowed rooms and improvised festivals — a marker of a community that has stopped seeing itself as temporary and started laying down roots in brick and stone.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: NRIs Sent India a Record $135 Billion. The Catch: Wiring Money the Old Way Quietly Skims Billions Off the Top.
nri-world.excerpt: India is the world's largest remittance recipient by a mile, but a thicket of new tax forms and stubbornly high bank-wire fees mean the diaspora keeps leaving money on the table.
nri-world.image_caption: Indian rupee notes and coins, the destination of a record $135 billion in diaspora remittances
nri-world.nri_angle: Every NRI who sends money home is part of this $135 billion flow — and most are losing 3-5% per transfer to fees and choosing the wrong account type, even as Delhi piles on fresh compliance paperwork they will have to navigate.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: An Immigrant Now Runs One of Manhattan's Most Closely Watched Neighborhoods. A 250-Year-Old Award Just Made the Point.
nri-world.excerpt: Raju Mann, the India-born head of New York's Battery Park City Authority, was honored at Federal Hall among five naturalized citizens recognized for shaping Lower Manhattan — a quiet marker of how far Indian-origin leadership has moved into the machinery of American cities.
nri-world.image_caption: Federal Hall National Memorial in Lower Manhattan, where the Alexander Hamilton Immigrant Achievement Awards are presented
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian-origin success in America has been told largely through the private economy — founders and CEOs. Raju Mann leading a major New York public authority, and being honored among naturalized citizens at Federal Hall, marks the diaspora's quieter move into civic stewardship: not just thriving in a city, but being trusted to govern part of it.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Most Powerful Old-Boys' Network in Tech Isn't From Stanford. It Just Turned 75 and Threw Itself a Party in California.
nri-world.excerpt: When thousands of IIT alumni gathered in Long Beach to mark 75 years of India's elite engineering schools, the real subject wasn't nostalgia. It was the question of what a diaspora network becomes once it stops needing to prove itself.
nri-world.image_caption: A campus of the Indian Institutes of Technology, which mark 75 years in 2026
nri-world.nri_angle: The IIT alumni network is among the most powerful pieces of diaspora infrastructure the world has built — the pipeline behind a generation of Indian-origin technology leaders in the US. Its 75th-anniversary gathering in California, courted by India's ambassador, captures the diaspora at a hinge: confident, courted by the homeland, and increasingly tilting capital and attention back toward India.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Procedure Can Reverse a Stroke in Minutes. Fewer Than 3% of the World Can Get It — and an Indian Doctor Has Spent a Decade Fixing That.
nri-world.excerpt: Dr. Dileep Yavagal, honored with a Lifetime Achievement Award at this year's American Academy of Neurology meeting, helped make clot removal a global standard. His harder fight is over who actually receives it — and in India, the answer is almost no one.
nri-world.image_caption: An interventional procedure in a catheterization suite; mechanical thrombectomy removes stroke-causing clots through a catheter
nri-world.nri_angle: Yavagal is the diaspora story less often told: not the founder or CEO, but the India-trained physician-scientist who reached the top of American medicine and turned it back toward the country he came from. India's ~1.4% access to a stroke treatment that can reverse disability — versus 32% in the US — is a gap that touches NRI families with aging parents in India directly.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Marry Out, and You Are Out: India's Top Court Weighs a Rule That Empties the Fire Temple of Its Daughters
nri-world.excerpt: A nine-judge bench has called the Parsi practice of excommunicating women who marry outside the faith “discriminatory.” For a community of barely 50,000 in India — and a scattered, shrinking diaspora — the stakes are nothing less than survival.
nri-world.image_caption: A Zoroastrian fire temple; India's Supreme Court is weighing whether barring Parsi women who marry outside the faith from such spaces is discriminatory
nri-world.nri_angle: Parsi/Zoroastrian communities are among the most globally dispersed of Indian-origin groups — Mumbai, London, Toronto, Sydney, Hong Kong, the US — and intensely affected by demographic decline. The Supreme Court's scrutiny of excommunicating women who marry outside the faith speaks directly to diaspora Zoroastrians, who face the same patriarchal membership rules in mixed marriages abroad, and whose North American federations remain split over recognising the children of intermarried members.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Diaspora Built Itself Around Its Children. Now It Is Building for Its Parents.
nri-world.excerpt: A new India Home senior centre opening in Hicksville on July 7 is a small ribbon-cutting with a large subtext: the first big wave of Indian immigrants to America is growing old, and the community is scrambling to catch up.
nri-world.image_caption: Elderly Indian women; as the first big wave of Indian immigrants to the US grows old, a new India Home senior centre opens in Hicksville, Long Island on July 7
nri-world.nri_angle: The first big wave of post-1965 Indian immigrants to the US is now entering old age, and culturally specific senior care — familiar food, language, festivals — is becoming one of the diaspora's most urgent and under-met needs. The Hicksville centre, replicating India Home's Queens model on suburban Long Island, signals a shift in diaspora priorities from arrival-and-aspiration institutions (temples, scholarships) toward institutions of permanence, with the same greying wave cresting from the Bay Area to Houston to Toronto and London.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: An Accenture Warning Knocks Indian IT — and the Bigger Fear Is What It Signals for Next Year
markets-finance.excerpt: After the world's largest IT services firm trimmed its revenue outlook, Indian software giants like Infosys, TCS and Wipro slid as much as 7 percent, and brokerages warned that the coming financial year could prove tougher than the market has been pricing in.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian IT majors slid sharply after Accenture trimmed its revenue guidance, dragging the Nifty IT index lower
markets-finance.nri_angle: Indian IT is the diaspora's bellwether industry — it employs many NRIs' relatives, anchors the portfolios of those who invest back home, and underpins the H-1B pipeline that brought a generation to America — so a warning that demand and AI are squeezing the sector touches NRI jobs, savings and family fortunes at once.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Faces Its Weakest Monsoon in 11 Years — but This Time the Economy Is Better Armoured
markets-finance.excerpt: A strengthening El Niño has delayed the rains and brought dangerous heat, threatening harvests, food prices and growth. Yet bigger reservoirs and far wider irrigation mean the damage may be more contained than the alarming headlines suggest.
markets-finance.image_caption: India faces its weakest monsoon in 11 years as a strengthening El Niño delays the rains and brings dangerous heat
markets-finance.nri_angle: A poor monsoon feeds straight into the things NRIs watch most closely about India — food inflation that erodes the rupee's value, the central bank's room to cut rates, and the strength of the currency their remittances and investments are denominated in — making this year's rains a quiet but real input into diaspora financial decisions.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Stock Exchange Is Going Public: NSE Files for a ₹30,000-Crore IPO, Set to Be the Country's Largest Ever
markets-finance.excerpt: After nearly a decade of regulatory delay, the National Stock Exchange has filed for a pure offer-for-sale of about 6% of its equity — a listing that would hand long-time backers like Azim Premji and Radhakishan Damani a multi-billion-dollar windfall.
markets-finance.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange has filed for a roughly ₹30,000-crore offer-for-sale, set to be India's largest-ever public issue
markets-finance.nri_angle: The exchange where most NRI portfolios are effectively built — through Indian mutual funds, direct equities and the derivatives market — is itself about to list, giving the diaspora both a marquee investment opportunity and a clearer window into how India's market plumbing is valued.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Gold Was Supposed to Soar During the Iran War. It Fell Nearly 10% Instead — Now JP Morgan Sees a 40% Rebound
markets-finance.excerpt: The metal that diaspora families trust as a crisis hedge defied its safe-haven reputation, sliding even as conflict raged, before steadying near ₹1.46 lakh per 10 grams. The episode is a sharp lesson in how gold really behaves — and why timing it is a fool's errand.
markets-finance.image_caption: Gold fell nearly 10% in India during the Iran war despite its safe-haven reputation, before steadying near ₹1.46 lakh per 10 grams
markets-finance.nri_angle: Gold is the diaspora's instinctive store of value — bought for weddings, gifted at festivals, hoarded as insurance against bad times — so its counter-intuitive slide during an actual war, and the debate over where it goes next, speaks directly to how NRIs should size and time their single most emotional investment.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The RBI Burned Through Nearly $9 Billion in a Single Month Defending the Rupee — and Reserves Are at a One-Year Low
markets-finance.excerpt: Fresh central bank data show the Reserve Bank of India sold a net $8.9 billion in April to slow the rupee's slide, capping a record fiscal year of intervention as foreign reserves fell to $671.6 billion and the currency clawed back from an all-time low.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India sold a net $8.9 billion in April to defend the rupee, with forex reserves falling to a one-year low
markets-finance.nri_angle: The scale of the RBI's dollar-selling tells NRIs how hard their central bank is working to keep the rupee from sliding further — a direct signal on the value of remittances, NRE and FCNR deposits, and India-bound investments, and on whether the recent record lows are a floor or a way station.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The Rupee Just Had Its Best Week in Months. Now a Resurgent Dollar Will Test Whether It Holds.
markets-finance.excerpt: A drop in oil after the US-Iran peace deal pushed the rupee to 94.32, its strongest weekly run in 11 weeks — but a dollar at a one-year high and a hawkish Federal Reserve are pulling the currency back, while government bonds wait on the pace of foreign money returning.
markets-finance.image_caption: The rupee posted its best week in months as oil prices fell, before a resurgent dollar tested the gains
markets-finance.nri_angle: Every move in the rupee reprices the remittances NRIs send home, the value of their NRE and FCNR deposits, and the returns on their Indian investments — so a week that swung from oil-driven relief to dollar-driven pressure is not abstract macro news for the diaspora but a direct signal on when to send money and what their India holdings are worth.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Ambani's Jio Files for What Could Be India's Biggest IPO Ever — and This Time, No One Is Cashing Out
markets-finance.excerpt: Jio Platforms has filed draft papers with India's markets regulator for a fresh-issue-only listing of up to 27 crore shares, a deal market estimates put near ₹36,000 crore at a valuation of roughly ₹12.5 lakh crore — with the proceeds aimed squarely at paying down debt rather than handing existing investors an exit.
markets-finance.image_caption: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani, whose Jio Platforms has filed draft papers for a record IPO
markets-finance.nri_angle: Jio touches nearly every Indian family with a phone, and its listing is the marquee event NRI investors have waited years for — a chance to own a slice of the diaspora's most-used digital utility, even as the fresh-issue-only structure and a cooled, war-rattled market raise real questions about price and timing.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: For Once, the Worry Is a Rate Hike: India's Central Bank Holds Steady as War-Driven Oil Tests Its Nerve
markets-finance.excerpt: Minutes of the June meeting show the RBI kept its key rate at 5.25 percent and chose to 'wait and watch' as an Iran-war oil spike sent the rupee tumbling and lifted its inflation forecast to 5.1 percent — even as some economists now bet the next move is up, not down, with HSBC penciling in half a point of hikes this year.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India held its key rate at 5.25 percent as a war-driven oil spike clouded the inflation outlook
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRIs sending money home, parking savings in Indian deposits or holding rupee assets, the prospect of rate hikes rather than cuts flips the usual calculus — it can lift returns on Indian fixed deposits and steady the rupee, but it also signals that war-driven inflation, not growth, is now the force steering India's monetary policy.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Foreigners Keep Selling Indian Stocks. Indians Keep Buying — and That Has Quietly Rewired the Market
markets-finance.excerpt: In May, foreign investors pulled nearly Rs 33,000 crore out of Indian equities while domestic institutions poured in over Rs 82,000 crore — powered by a record Rs 30,954 crore of monthly SIP contributions across 9.64 crore accounts — a structural shift that means the old reflex of watching foreign flows to call the market is increasingly out of date.
markets-finance.image_caption: Domestic mutual fund inflows have grown large enough to absorb foreign investors' selling of Indian equities
markets-finance.nri_angle: Many NRIs still read foreign-investor outflows as a sell signal for Indian stocks, but a steady tide of domestic SIP money is now large enough to absorb that selling — a shift that should reframe how the diaspora thinks about timing, volatility and where the Indian market's real support now comes from.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is Dangling Higher Dollar Rates to Pull NRI Money Home — and Banks Now Want to Route It Through GIFT City
markets-finance.excerpt: After the RBI agreed to absorb the hedging cost on fresh foreign-currency NRI deposits and scrapped the rate caps, banks have pushed dollar deposit rates to 6–7 percent and are seeking permission to fund the inflows through their offshore GIFT City units — part of a drive analysts think could draw $55 billion or more to steady the rupee.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India has sweetened terms on foreign-currency NRI deposits to draw the diaspora's dollars and steady the rupee
markets-finance.nri_angle: This drive is aimed squarely at the diaspora's wallet: NRIs can suddenly earn 6–7 percent on dollar deposits in Indian banks — nearly double the old rates and with no currency risk — making it one of the most consequential personal-finance shifts for overseas Indians in years.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is Courting Foreign Bond Money — but the RBI Wants It Trading at Home, Not Through Euroclear
markets-finance.excerpt: Even after scrapping taxes to lure overseas investors into its government bonds, India's central bank is resisting offshore settlement platforms like Euroclear, insisting foreigners trade directly on the domestic system to keep the market's liquidity in one place.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India wants foreign investors to trade its government bonds on the domestic NDS-OM platform rather than via offshore systems
markets-finance.nri_angle: How freely foreign money flows into India's $1-trillion-plus government bond market shapes the rupee, India's borrowing costs and the stability of the assets NRIs hold back home — so the central bank's careful, on-its-own-terms opening of the market is a quiet signal about the financial backdrop against which the diaspora invests, remits and plans for retirement in India.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Tax Tribunal Says Money NRIs Send Into Their NRE Accounts From Foreign Salaries Cannot Be Taxed as 'Unexplained' Income
markets-finance.excerpt: An income-tax appellate ruling has deleted a tax demand against a non-resident Indian, holding that once funds in an NRE account are shown to come from foreign earnings, the tax department cannot treat them as unexplained money — a quiet but meaningful protection for the diaspora.
markets-finance.image_caption: India's tax tribunal ruled that foreign-salary credits in an NRI's NRE account cannot be taxed as unexplained income
markets-finance.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs route their overseas salaries into NRE accounts in India to support family, buy property or invest — and the fear of a tax notice questioning those inflows is real, so a tribunal confirming that genuinely foreign-earned money parked in an NRE account is not taxable removes a recurring anxiety for the diaspora.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Eleven Balls: A 15-Year-Old Just Broke the Fastest-Fifty Record in 50-Over Cricket
sports.excerpt: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi reached his half-century in 11 deliveries for India A against Sri Lanka A in Dambulla, the quickest in the history of List A cricket — a record-breaking innings of 94 off 29 days before the teenager is set to become India's youngest ever men's international.
sports.image_caption: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, the 15-year-old who hit the fastest fifty in List A history
sports.nri_angle: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is the prodigy the entire cricket-following diaspora is tracking — his record 11-ball fifty comes just as he is named for India's tours of Ireland and England, putting a likely record-breaking debut within reach of NRI crowds and making him the must-watch name of the summer.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Five Hundreds Were Not Enough: England Chase 371 at Headingley, and India's New Era Opens With a Defeat
sports.excerpt: Ben Duckett's brilliant 149 carried England to 373 for 5 and a five-wicket win on the final day, leaving India the first team in Test history to lose a match in which it scored five individual centuries — a chastening start to Shubman Gill's captaincy.
sports.image_caption: Ben Duckett, whose 149 powered England's chase of 371 at Headingley
sports.nri_angle: A new India era under captain Shubman Gill — the first Test of the post-Kohli, post-Rohit transition — opened with a wrenching defeat despite five individual centuries. For the large British-Indian crowd at Headingley and NRIs watching across the US, Canada and the Gulf, it was a sobering, unforgettable start to a new chapter of the team they follow most closely.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: MI New York Found Their Feet in Texas, and an Edison-Raised Captain Led the Way Home
sports.excerpt: A night after their season opened with a stumble, the Mumbai Indians' American franchise dismantled the Texas Super Kings for 158 and chased it down with eight wickets to spare — USA captain Monank Patel anchoring, Nicholas Pooran finishing unbeaten on 68.
sports.image_caption: Trent Boult, who took 3 for 18 to help bowl out the Texas Super Kings for 158
sports.nri_angle: Major League Cricket is the competition the Indian-American community helped build, and MI New York's first win of 2026 was anchored by Monank Patel — the New Jersey-raised USA captain — a hometown hero for NRIs following top-tier T20 cricket on American soil.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Three Centuries, One Collapse: India Pile Up 471 at Headingley, Then Watch England Punch Straight Back
sports.excerpt: Yashasvi Jaiswal, Shubman Gill and Rishabh Pant all reached three figures on a sun-soaked Leeds morning — yet India lost their last seven wickets for 41, and by stumps Ollie Pope's unbeaten hundred had England right back in the contest.
sports.image_caption: Rishabh Pant, whose stylish 134 was the highlight of India's first innings at Headingley
sports.nri_angle: The first Test of India's post-Kohli, post-Rohit era is captivating the diaspora: three hometown heroes — Jaiswal, captain Gill and the inspirational comeback man Rishabh Pant — all scored hundreds at Headingley, yet a classic lower-order collapse kept England in the game, a drama NRIs across the US, UK and Canada are following ball by ball.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: No Indian in the Singles Again: At Wimbledon, the Flag Now Travels in the Doubles Draw
sports.excerpt: As Wimbledon qualifying began this week, India had no man or woman in any Grand Slam singles main draw for a second straight year. The tricolour at SW19 will be carried by its doubles specialists — and, in a twist, by an Indian-American who could never play for India.
sports.image_caption: Yuki Bhambri, India's top-ranked doubles player, leads a doubles-only Indian contingent at Wimbledon 2026
sports.nri_angle: For a second straight year no Indian features in Grand Slam singles, so the tricolour at Wimbledon travels in the doubles draw — carried by an Indian Army subedar in the form of his life and a veteran reborn in the two-man game — while the diaspora's biggest SW19 story is Rajeev Ram, the Indian-American former World No. 1 who once tried, and failed, to play for India.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: One Defeat Turned India's World Cup Into a Tightrope: Beat Australia, or Trust a Calculator
sports.excerpt: A shock loss to South Africa has stripped away India's safety net at the Women's T20 World Cup. Harmanpreet Kaur's side must now get past Bangladesh and the six-time champions to be sure of the semi-finals.
sports.image_caption: India captain Harmanpreet Kaur, whose side must navigate a virtual knockout to reach the semi-finals
sports.nri_angle: The Indian women's team has become appointment viewing across the diaspora, and its June 28 virtual knockout against Australia at Lord's — a ground steeped in NRI pilgrimage — is the sort of fixture that fills WhatsApp groups from London to New Jersey, with a generation of diaspora girls now growing up on Harmanpreet and Mandhana.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Sacked the Captain Who Won Them the T20 World Cup — and Left Him Out of the Team Altogether
sports.excerpt: Months after Suryakumar Yadav lifted India's third T20 world title, the selectors have stripped him of the captaincy and his place in the side. Shreyas Iyer, back in the format after two and a half years, inherits the job.
sports.image_caption: Shreyas Iyer, recalled after more than two years, is India's new full-time T20I captain
sports.nri_angle: A World Cup-winning captain dropped months after the trophy lift is a Rorschach test for the diaspora — cold-blooded modernity to some, betrayal to others — and a window on how ruthless India have become about staying atop the white-ball game, the kind of loyalty-versus-results debate that runs hot in NRI WhatsApp groups across time zones.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Picked Its England One-Day Squad, and the Team Sheet Read Like a Changing of the Guard
sports.excerpt: Shubman Gill now captains India in all three formats, Jasprit Bumrah is back, and Yashasvi Jaiswal was left out despite a match-winning hundred. Virat Kohli is in too — if his hamstring lets him be.
sports.image_caption: Shubman Gill, who now captains India across all three formats, will lead the ODI side in England
sports.nri_angle: A squad sheet that captures a generational handover the diaspora has followed with tenderness — the team passing from Kohli and Rohit to Shubman Gill, who now captains across all formats — while the dropping of a centurion (Jaiswal) is exactly the kind of selection debate that lights up NRI WhatsApp groups across time zones, all framed against India's build toward the 2027 ODI World Cup.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Seventeen Years After Her First Match in England, Harmanpreet Kaur Walked Out for Her 200th — a Number No Cricketer Had Ever Reached
sports.excerpt: India's captain became the first player, man or woman, to appear in 200 T20 Internationals. That it happened at a World Cup in the same country where she debuted as a teenager in 2009 made the milestone read like a story written in advance.
sports.image_caption: Harmanpreet Kaur, India's captain and the first cricketer to play 200 T20 Internationals
sports.nri_angle: Harmanpreet Kaur is one of the players through whom the Indian diaspora embraced the women's game, and her 17-year climb to a record 200 T20Is mirrors the rise of women's cricket in India that NRIs have followed with growing pride — a story of persistence rewarded that resonates across a community built on long journeys far from home.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's Most Famous Paddler Missed the Asian Games Team by One Ranking Place
sports.excerpt: Manika Batra, the face of Indian table tennis, has been named only a reserve: world No. 51, one spot short of the top-50 ranking that would have guaranteed her a place. Her public appeal to the Prime Minister has reopened an old fight over how India picks its athletes.
sports.image_caption: Manika Batra receiving the Arjuna Award in 2018
sports.nri_angle: Manika Batra is one of the few Indian Olympic-sport athletes with genuine global recognition, and the row over whether a transparent ranking rule should override proven international pedigree strikes a familiar chord with NRIs who follow India's Olympic-sport rise and value merit-based process.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Europe Just Launched Its First Big-League T20 — and the Diaspora Built Half the Talent Pool
sports.excerpt: The ICC-sanctioned European T20 Premier League opened its player draft this week, with six city franchises across Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands — cricketing nations whose teams the South Asian diaspora has quietly powered for years.
sports.image_caption: Malahide Cricket Ground in Dublin, one of Ireland's international venues; the new ETPL will field two Irish franchises, in Dublin and Belfast
sports.nri_angle: The Irish, Scottish and Dutch national teams the ETPL is built to strengthen have for years been substantially powered by South Asian immigrant communities, and a serious, well-broadcast home league gives diaspora families across Britain, Ireland and the Netherlands a top-tier local team to watch and a real professional pathway for their children.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: A Smaller India Heads to Glasgow — and the Sports It Wins Most Aren't on the Bill
sports.excerpt: India will send just 125-130 athletes and staff to a stripped-down Commonwealth Games that has dropped wrestling, badminton, hockey and table tennis — its richest medal seams.
sports.image_caption: Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu, one of India's medal hopes in a Glasgow programme that retains weightlifting
sports.nri_angle: The Commonwealth Games have long been the most accessible stage for Indians in Britain, Canada and Australia to watch their country compete, and Glasgow's stripped-down programme — minus India's signature sports of badminton, wrestling and hockey — means fewer of those moments, even as Ahmedabad's 2030 Games promise to bring the event home.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Accenture Just Had Its Worst Week on Record. The Fear Driving It Lands Hardest on Indian IT.
technology.excerpt: A cautious outlook and shrinking bookings wiped a quarter off Accenture's value. Wall Street is now treating the whole IT-services model — TCS, Infosys and Wipro included — as a thing AI might eat.
technology.image_caption: Accenture's office complex in Gachibowli, Hyderabad, one of its largest delivery hubs in India
technology.nri_angle: For the Indian engineer at a US IT-services firm and the NRI holding TCS or Infosys shares, Accenture's selloff is the clearest signal yet that AI is being priced as a threat to the entire outsourcing model, not a tailwind.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Tesla Now Has Five Showrooms in India and Almost No Sales. The Real Test Starts This Summer.
technology.excerpt: Hyderabad and Bengaluru just joined Mumbai and Delhi on Tesla's India map. But 100% import duties mean a Model Y costs nearly $70,000 — and only 350 have sold.
technology.image_caption: The 2026 Tesla Model Y, the company's lead model for the Indian market
technology.nri_angle: NRIs who own Tesla stock or are eyeing a move back to India get a live case study in whether a premium American brand can crack a price-obsessed market choked by import tariffs.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Adobe's Indian-Born CEO Spent 18 Years Building a Subscription Empire. On His Way Out, He's Tearing Up the Playbook.
technology.excerpt: Shantanu Narayen is leaving Adobe with a parting bet: give the AI tools away free, monetise later. Wall Street isn't sure his successor can pull it off.
technology.image_caption: Shantanu Narayen, the outgoing chief executive of Adobe Inc.
technology.nri_angle: Narayen is one of the original Indian-origin CEOs who made Silicon Valley's executive suite look like Hyderabad; how his AI-era succession plays out is a referendum on whether that generation's playbook survives the agentic shift.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Oracle Just Cut 21,000 Jobs in a Year — Its Biggest Purge Ever. The Filing Names AI as the Reason.
technology.excerpt: The database giant shed 13% of its workforce to bankroll a $70 billion AI data-centre spree. For Indian engineers on H-1B visas, the safe seat is now on the team building the machines, not maintaining the software.
technology.image_caption: Oracle's corporate headquarters towers in Redwood City, California
technology.nri_angle: Oracle's US and India campuses run heavily on Indian H-1B and L-1 talent, and the cuts hit legacy-software teams hardest while sparing AI and cloud — a stark signal for NRI engineers deciding where to sit.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Trump Wants a Working Quantum Computer by 2028 — Sooner Than IBM Plans One. Indian Talent Is Already in the Race.
technology.excerpt: Two executive orders fast-track a national quantum machine and an encryption overhaul. The funded workforce push is a hiring surge for exactly the STEM graduates the diaspora supplies — and India is running its own version.
technology.image_caption: An IBM quantum computer on display at a technology summit in Delhi
technology.nri_angle: Quantum sits at the physics-engineering-CS crossroads where Indian-origin researchers are heavily represented, and a federally funded workforce push plus India's own National Quantum Mission make this a two-country opportunity for NRIs.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's IT Giants Promised a Better Year in April. Three Months In, Analysts Already See FY27 Slipping.
technology.excerpt: AI automation and the West Asia war are squeezing TCS, Infosys, Wipro and peers, whose shares are down 30% in 2026. For NRIs, it's both a bruised portfolio and a worry about family inside the Bengaluru campuses.
technology.image_caption: The glass pyramid at the Infosys campus in Bengaluru, India
technology.nri_angle: Many NRIs hold Indian IT stocks directly and have relatives working inside these campuses, so the AI-driven squeeze on the $315 billion sector is at once a portfolio question and a family one.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Arvind Krishna Spent Years Calling IBM an AI Company. Now He's Buying OpenAI's Help to Prove It.
technology.excerpt: IBM joined OpenAI's cyber program and put a $5 billion bet behind securing the world's open-source code. For Indian engineers in security and consulting, it redraws where the jobs are.
technology.image_caption: IBM Chairman and CEO Arvind Krishna speaking at SXSW in 2025
technology.nri_angle: IBM's pivot to AI-driven application security reshapes the career math for the tens of thousands of Indian engineers in its security, consulting and Bengaluru delivery arms, even as CEO Arvind Krishna warns the broader AI buildout may be a bubble.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Every Tech CEO Is Pouring Billions Into AI Data Centres. The Founder of India's Biggest SaaS Firm Says He'll Sit It Out.
technology.excerpt: Sridhar Vembu calls the AI buildout a bubble, ships a made-in-India ERP, and rules out an IPO again. His pitch to NRIs is unusually direct: come home.
technology.image_caption: Zoho Corporation's headquarters in Chennai, India
technology.nri_angle: Zoho's bootstrapped, no-IPO, build-it-in-India playbook is a direct counter-pitch to the venture-and-equity model most NRI tech workers know, and Vembu is explicitly inviting Indian engineers abroad to return and build.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Washington Cut Off Anthropic's Best AI Models to Foreign Nationals Overnight. Indian Engineers Just Learned Who Owns the Switch.
technology.excerpt: A single export-control letter pulled Fable 5 and Mythos 5 from everyone, including Anthropic's own foreign-born staff. For India's AI workforce, the lesson is about dependence.
technology.image_caption: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei at TechCrunch Disrupt in 2023
technology.nri_angle: The export ban barred foreign nationals — a category that includes a large share of Indian engineers at US AI labs and the millions of Indian developers who build on frontier models — exposing how quickly access to critical AI can vanish.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Every Big Tech Firm Is Cutting H-1B Hiring. Nvidia Just Doubled Down — and Indians Are the Reason.
technology.excerpt: While Google and Amazon slashed visa sponsorships by up to 40%, Jensen Huang's chipmaker added certifications and pay packages that read like a different economy entirely.
technology.image_caption: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, whose company expanded H-1B hiring while rivals pulled back
technology.nri_angle: For Indian engineers who hold roughly 71-73% of US H-1B visas, Nvidia's counter-cyclical hiring is the rare safe harbour in a market where a layoff now triggers a brutal 60-day deadline to find a new sponsor.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Forbes Just Named the 50 Hottest AI Startups. Six Are Run by Indian Americans.
technology.excerpt: From a cardiologist's medical-scribe tool to the open-source lab behind RedPajama, the diaspora's footprint on Forbes' AI 50 is no longer a curiosity — it's a pattern.
technology.nri_angle: For NRIs deciding whether to join a startup, fund one, or send a resume, the AI 50 is a map of where Indian-American founders are building the most fundable companies in the most competitive sector on earth.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: A Ransomware Gang Says It Stole Apple and Tesla Secrets — From a Tata Plant in India.
technology.excerpt: Tata Electronics confirms a 'cybersecurity incident' as a leak group dumps 200,000 files, in the latest crack to appear in India's bid to become the West's factory floor.
technology.image_caption: Code on a screen during a cybersecurity incident; a leak group dumped files it tied to Tata Electronics
technology.nri_angle: For NRIs invested in India's manufacturing story — and for engineers building the supply chain that lets Apple make iPhones outside China — a breach at its flagship contract manufacturer is a direct test of whether 'Make in India' can be trusted with the world's most valuable trade secrets.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.excerpt: He gave NRIs their loudest patriotic roar with Gadar 2. Now Sunny Deol teams with Gopichand Malineni, S Thaman and Mythri Movie Makers for SDGM — and the only words on the poster are 'Mass Feast Loading.'

entertainment.excerpt: Fourteen inmates, six weeks, and a confessional that has already produced the year's most unhinged press launch. Sach Ya Sazaa storms Netflix on June 27.

entertainment.title: The Doctor Returns to Bhathkandi. 'Gram Chikitsalay' Season 2 Quietly Lands on Prime Video — and It Might Be TVF's Warmest Show Yet.
entertainment.excerpt: No item songs, no spy universe, no ₹100-crore weekend. Just Amol Parashar's idealistic doctor, a crumbling village clinic, and a second season that streams worldwide from June 23.

entertainment.excerpt: 'Rooh' reunites the genre's most recognisable face with the 'Breathe' director for a big-screen musical-horror spectacle, releasing pan-India in 2027.

entertainment.title: A Golden Lotus, a Stolen Temple, and No Star to Sell It. 'Nagabandham' Is Betting Everything on Spectacle.
entertainment.excerpt: Abhishek Nama's mythological epic dropped its Hindi trailer with no A-lister on the poster — just Naga Sadhus, a 5,000-dancer set piece, and a budget that swelled five times over. It arrives July 3, and it is the most fascinating gamble of the summer.

entertainment.title: Janhvi Kapoor Just Made Eyewear a Flex. POP MART's First India Drop Lands on Her Face — and the Diaspora's Wishlist.
entertainment.excerpt: The actress fronted Lenskart's launch of the viral Labubu maker's debut Indian collection — 21 frames built on the 'I Want A Hug' universe, blind-box charms and all. It's the most on-brand celebrity tie-up of the year.
entertainment.image_caption: Janhvi Kapoor, who fronts the POP MART x Lenskart India launch (Wikimedia Commons)

entertainment.title: Shah Rukh Khan Takes Back Christmas — and Brings Suhana With Him. 'King' Locks December 25.
entertainment.excerpt: SRK plays a lethal assassin, his daughter plays his protégé, and a 45-day gap from 'Ramayana' clears the runway for the comeback the diaspora has been waiting three years for.
entertainment.image_caption: Promotional poster for King, releasing December 25, 2026 (Wikipedia)

entertainment.title: Ranveer Singh Is Fighting Zombies. Vicky Kaushal Is Becoming a God. Bollywood's Next Bench Just Made Its Biggest Bets.
entertainment.excerpt: Ranveer blocks August for the ₹300-crore zombie epic 'Pralay' — and turns producer — while Vicky surrenders 18 months to play Parashurama in 'Mahavatar'. The biggest swings aren't coming from the marquee names anymore.

entertainment.excerpt: Arjun, Janhvi, Khushi and Shanaya gathered for a Mata Ki Chowki as Boney Kapoor's daughter kicks off a July wedding — and the 1:15 AM love story behind it is melting the internet.

entertainment.title: Allu Arjun Faces the Court From a Mumbai Film Set. The Pushpa 2 Stampede Case Catches Up With the Pan-India Star.
entertainment.excerpt: Named 'Accused No. 11' over the death that shadowed his biggest hit, the Telugu superstar appeared virtually before Hyderabad's Nampally Court — and the hearing was deferred again.

lifestyle-health.title: One of the Biggest Risks for Dementia Is Also One of the Easiest to Treat — and It Sits in the Ears
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new analysis of more than 16,000 American adults found severe hearing loss was associated with a sharply higher risk of dementia, while a major randomized trial showed that simply fitting at-risk elders with hearing aids slowed their cognitive decline by nearly half.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Researchers found fitting at-risk older adults with hearing aids cut their rate of cognitive decline by nearly half
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: In many Indian families, an elder's fading hearing is quietly accepted as a normal part of getting old and rarely treated — yet this research reframes an untreated hearing problem as a serious, fixable threat to the mind, making a hearing test and a pair of hearing aids one of the most worthwhile gifts an NRI child can arrange for a parent ageing in India or abroad.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Scientists Have Found Microplastics Inside the Human Eye — and the More There Were, the Higher the Pressure
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In the first study to look, researchers detected microplastic particles in every sample of a delicate drainage tissue taken from glaucoma patients, and the plastic burden tracked closely with the dangerously high eye pressure that drives the disease.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Scientists detected microplastic particles in the eye's fluid-draining tissue, linked to higher intraocular pressure in glaucoma patients
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Glaucoma is a leading cause of irreversible blindness in India, and the diaspora hails from some of the most plastic-saturated, air-polluted cities on earth — so early evidence that plastic particles may lodge in the eye and push up the pressure that steals sight is a story that lands close to home for millions of NRI families.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Weakness That Comes With Age May Live as Much in the Brain as in the Muscle, a New Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: When researchers gave older adults a jolt of electrical stimulation at the moment they thought they were pushing as hard as they could, the weakest among them produced far more force — a sign that ageing nerves, not just shrinking muscle, may be holding strength back.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A study of 66 older adults found weaker participants had untapped muscle strength their nervous systems were not fully activating
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: For NRI families caring for ageing parents across continents — often advising on health by video call — the finding reframes the goal from simply lifting weights to keeping the brain-to-muscle connection sharp, suggesting that balance work, coordination and learning new movements deserve a place alongside resistance training in the routines that keep elders independent.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: People on Ozempic-Style Drugs Are Moving Less, Not More — and Doctors Say That Undercuts the Benefit
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A study of 753 adults using fitness-tracker data found that daily steps and exercise actually fell after people started GLP-1 weight-loss medications, raising the risk that muscle is lost along with fat unless physical activity is built in deliberately.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A study of 753 adults found daily steps and exercise fell after people began GLP-1 weight-loss medications
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: GLP-1 drugs have spread fast among diaspora Indians battling the high rates of diabetes and obesity that run in South Asian families, and this finding is a pointed warning — for a group already prone to losing muscle and storing dangerous fat, taking the medication without keeping up movement risks trading one health problem for another.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: How Fit You Are in Midlife May Forecast How Long — and How Well — You Live, a 24,000-Person Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Adults with higher cardiorespiratory fitness measured on a treadmill in midlife went on to live longer, fall ill less often and stretch out their healthy years, according to a large analysis published in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A 24,576-adult study found that higher cardiorespiratory fitness in midlife was linked to a longer life span and fewer diseases
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry an outsized burden of heart disease and diabetes, often at lower body weights than other groups, and aerobic fitness is one of the few levers that pushes back on both — making this evidence that a midlife habit of brisk movement can buy healthy years especially relevant to NRI families.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Body's ‘Biological Age’ May Start Falling in Just Four Weeks on a Plant-Forward Diet, a New Trial Suggests
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Older adults who shifted toward complex carbohydrates and more plant-based foods narrowed the gap between their biological and chronological age within a month — a sign that the body's ageing markers can move surprisingly fast.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A four-week trial found that shifting toward plant-forward, complex-carbohydrate diets narrowed the gap between biological and chronological age
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Traditional Indian cooking is already built around the plant-forward, complex-carbohydrate foods this trial favoured — lentils, vegetables, whole grains and legumes — meaning many diaspora families are a few deliberate swaps, not a wholesale overhaul, away from a diet linked to younger biological ageing.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Health Benefits of Coffee May Hinge on the Clock: Morning Drinkers Lived Longer in a 40,000-Person Study
lifestyle-health.excerpt: People who confined their coffee to the hours before noon had the sharpest reductions in death from any cause — and from heart disease — while all-day sippers saw no such benefit, a large U.S. analysis published in the European Heart Journal found.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A large U.S. study found that adults who drank coffee only in the morning had lower rates of death than all-day drinkers
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Coffee and chai are woven into the rhythm of Indian and diaspora households — the morning cup, the evening catch-up, the late-night work fuel — and this research suggests that simply pulling caffeine earlier in the day, rather than giving it up, may be the cheapest longevity tweak an NRI can make.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: More Than 1 in 3 Older Adults Fall Short on Protein — and Vegetarians and Meal-Skippers Are Most at Risk
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Despite a cultural obsession with high-protein everything, large dietary surveys keep finding that a third or more of adults over 50 miss the mark — a shortfall tied to weaker muscles, more frailty and poorer diets overall, and one that hits plant-forward eaters hardest.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Lentils, beans and other legumes are dense, affordable protein sources, key for older adults and vegetarians at risk of falling short
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: A large share of the Indian diaspora eats vegetarian or near-vegetarian, leans on carbohydrate-heavy staples like rice and roti, and skips or front-loads meals around busy work and fasting schedules — exactly the pattern that leaves older adults short on protein and vulnerable to muscle loss, making this a quietly urgent issue in NRI homes.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Bacteria in Your Mouth Help Beetroot Lower Blood Pressure — and It Works Best as You Age
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Two new studies show that nitrate-rich vegetables like beetroot reshape the oral microbiome to ease blood pressure in older adults, and that a surprising trick — chewing ordinary sugary gum — can amplify the effect.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Nitrate-rich beetroot lowers blood pressure with the help of bacteria in the mouth, and the effect is strongest in older adults (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: High blood pressure is one of the most common and dangerous chronic conditions in the Indian diaspora, and the foods at the heart of this research — beetroot, leafy greens and other nitrate-rich vegetables — are already fixtures of the South Asian kitchen, offering NRI families a low-cost, drug-free lever that grows more effective with age.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Lesser-Known Estrogen Made in Body Fat May Explain Why Obesity Drives Breast Cancer After Menopause
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Scientists are zeroing in on estrone, a hormone churned out by fat tissue, as a hidden engine of postmenopausal breast cancer — and the finding helps explain why weight, and the new generation of weight-loss drugs, may matter more for risk than once thought.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Researchers are focusing on estrone, an estrogen produced by body fat, to explain why obesity raises postmenopausal breast cancer risk
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian women carry a rising burden of both central obesity and breast cancer that often strikes earlier than in Western populations, yet awareness of the link between body fat and hormone-driven tumors remains low in many diaspora households — making the science of estrone a timely, actionable nudge toward waistline and metabolic health, not just mammograms.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Diet Built to Lower Blood Pressure Just Beat Five Rivals at Protecting the Aging Brain
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a Harvard-led comparison of nearly 160,000 people, the DASH eating pattern outperformed the Mediterranean diet and four others, with the most faithful followers showing a 41 percent lower risk of cognitive decline decades later.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A Harvard-led study found the DASH eating pattern was the strongest dietary predictor of late-life cognitive health
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face an unusually high burden of both hypertension and dementia, yet the brain-protective DASH pattern — heavy on vegetables, fruit, whole grains, beans and low-fat dairy, light on salt and sweets — maps neatly onto a thoughtfully built Indian thali, giving NRI families a culturally familiar template that may guard the heart and the mind at once.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: People Born With Naturally Lower Cholesterol Are Far Less Likely to Develop Dementia, a Million-Person Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Using genetics to sidestep the bias of ordinary diet studies, researchers found that a modest lifelong reduction in cholesterol — the same effect statins aim for — was linked to a sharply lower risk of dementia, hinting that protecting the heart may also protect the mind.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A study of more than a million people linked genetically lower cholesterol to a sharply reduced risk of dementia
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry both elevated heart-disease risk and a high genetic predisposition to unhealthy cholesterol, and statins are already among the most prescribed drugs in Indian households — so evidence that lifelong lower cholesterol may also guard against dementia gives the diaspora one more reason to take a number they were already told to watch seriously.
